title: Fire Master Plan 2023–2032 approved
subtitle: Low-risk home food kitchens zoning change, Bridgeport and Margaret park funding, and a December closed training session.
overview: Council approved the Fire Master Plan, 2023-2032 {{vote:m4}}. It directs staff to bring forward recommendations with budget implications in the 2024-2026 budget and 2027 as a service level increase. Staff and the firefighters' association said growth, rising call volumes and high-rise intensification are putting pressure on response capacity. Fire station options, including flood risk at Station 1, are still under review, with an update expected in the new year.

Council also approved a zoning amendment allowing low-risk home food kitchens, such as home bakeries in a secondary kitchen, as a permitted home occupation {{vote:m5}}. These businesses will need a licence, and the food must be consumed off site. Council released 2023 capital funding of $421,000 for the Bridgeport and Margaret park project {{vote:m3}}, and received a drinking water management review for information {{vote:m2}}.

Council will attend a closed regional education and training session on December 8 {{vote:m6}}. Members also marked the International Day of Persons with Disabilities and remembered former Councillor Morty Taylor. The Mayor reported on an economic development mission to Germany.

decisions.detail: Council approved the plan and its next-step actions, and directed staff to bring budget-related recommendations forward in the 2024-2026 and 2027 budgets as a service level increase.
Council approved Zoning By-law Amendment Z-23-11 permitting low-risk food kitchens as a home occupation under By-law 2018-050.
Council approved releasing $421,000 in 2023 capital funding for the Bridgeport and Margaret park project.
Council received the drinking water quality management system review report for information.
Council agreed to attend a closed all-council education and training meeting on December 8, 2023.

debate: A fire association delegate supported the plan and said current staffing does not meet the standard for high-rise responses. Staff said the plan will not reach that level and relies on mutual aid and training.

Councillors asked whether the plan prepares for hazards such as electric vehicle battery fires and for firefighter contamination risks. Staff described new equipment, training and a gear-hygiene program.

Several councillors asked about Station 1 flood risk and whether a new west-side station is needed. Staff said a new build remains an option, while another crew at Station 2 would put more firefighters on scene sooner.

One councillor asked whether the chief training officer position could start sooner than the plan's schedule. Staff said it is being actively discussed, and that mechanical maintenance was given priority.

On home kitchens, councillors asked about food volume, waste and health inspections. Staff said licensing can address waste and that public health inspections are triggered by licence applications. One councillor suggested fire safety education for applicants.
